messages:
maria: FYI: SOC needs a timeboxed export of masked auth logs for incident #420. Scope: 2026-03-18 00:00 -> 2026-03-18 06:00 UTC. Purpose: triage for suspicious token reuse. Asking for 72h TTL on the export, KMS unwrap for one-time access, and group-limited download (soc-triage team).
alek: questions: who will request unwrap and how do we ensure the unwrap is auditable? also, is masking sufficient (hashing user ids) or do we need redaction?
maria: unwrap by SOC lead only (manual approval ticket + audit hook). Masking preferred: keep PII hashed with salt, leave IPs intact for correlation. We want to avoid full redaction unless legal asks.
tariq: recommend JIT decryption sessions using our ephemeral-kms-proxy. Flow: create export blob encrypted with customer-managed KMS, generate time-limited decryption token (TTL 72h), log token issuance to audit pipeline. That keeps KMS keys safe and provides audit trail.
sam: implementer note: exporter job can write to s3://redwood-temp-exports/incident-420/ then trigger kms-proxy to wrap key. Need a post-export lambda to apply lifecycle policy: delete after 72h + 1hr buffer. Anyone object to automation + TTL enforcement?
alek: sounds good. small ask: include an allowlist for IPs that can download, and require download via signed URL that checks group membership (soc-triage) against our IDP at request time.
maria: agreed. we also need a ticket template for approvals so SOC lead attaches justification + analyst list. put template in the ticketing system (ops folder).
oncall-bot: Deploy checklist: 1) Create export job (PR) 2) Add KMS policy entry: "allow kms:Decrypt" for kms-proxy-service 3) Add S3 bucket lifecycle rule 4) Create IAM group soc-triage and attach s3:GetObject + signed-url constraint 5) Link ticket ID to export job.
maria: putting checklist items in #incidents and creating ticket now. tagging @alek for KMS policy change.
alek: will draft the KMS policy. sample snippet below for the ephemeral grant (pseudo-AWS IAM):
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01",
  "Condition": {
    "DateLessThan": {"aws:CurrentTime": "2026-03-21T12:00:00Z"},
    "StringEquals": {"kms:CallerUserGroup": "soc-triage"}
  }
}
```
sam: we'll validate that DateLessThan is set dynamically by the proxy (TTL 72h). Also add an auditor-only role that can view audit entries but cannot unwrap.
maria: one more: retention policy for the SIEM export index — ensure we don't double-retain. The exported blob is for triage only; ingestion into external SIEM is forbidden unless legal approves. Add a sticky header in the object metadata: `x-export-intent: triage-only`.
tariq: automation tip: exporter job should tag objects with `expiry=2026-03-21T09:15:00Z` and we should have a periodic job to delete expired items plus a verification run that logs deletions to the security audit index.
alek: will add an additional KMS key usage metric to the telemetry so we can alert on unexpected decrypt patterns.
maria: approvals: @tariq you + @alek please ack once PRs are created. SOC lead will request unwrap via ticket. Need a quick runbook for oncall in case export contains PII by mistake.
oncall-bot: Runbook stub created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/export-triage (add details before go-live)
sam: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4162 (exporter + lifecycle) — reviews welcome
alek: KMS policy PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2091 — includes ephemeral proxy condition + auditor role
maria: 👍 thanks everyone. I'll update the incident ticket and post final checklist here when PRs are merged. Closing loop: keep all download attempts logged to the security audit index and retain those logs per retention policy (90d internal, then archive masked).
alek: acked
tariq: acked
sam: acked :thumbsup:"
